name: H5N1 bird flu
value: US H5N1 death (1 Nov); no human spread
summary: Washington State reports first US H5N1 death of 2026; no person-to-person spread
state: A Yakima County, Washington, resident with prior health conditions who was exposed to infected dairy cattle died of H5N1 on 1 Nov (PBS, 2 Nov). The CDC found no genetic changes making spread easier and rates public risk low; three human infections are linked to dairy exposure there, and contacts are being monitored.
for_you: Avoid contact with sick or dead birds and livestock; risk to the public is low (CDC).
rubric_hit: No human clusters or human-to-human spread

sources.title: PBS NewsHour — Washington resident dies from bird flu
Contagion Live — Washington reports first US avian influenza death of 2026

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.

rubric.watch: Human clusters under investigation, rising human cases, or new mammalian species spread.
